To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the level of public support for long-term care (i.e., the means test), which is a function of the recipient’s wealth, the cost of care, the amount of insurance benefits received, or a combination of the three, affects the relationship between the level of insurance and the level of informal care.

(1) the optimal level of informal care decreases when the public support structure takes into account LTC needs and/or insurance benefits; (2) the optimal level for insurance benefits decreases when the public scheme takes into account the insurance benefits; and (3) when the public support scheme takes into account LTC costs and insurance benefits, the optimal insurance benefit level increases when the level of informal care increases.

the optimal levels for insurance and informal care are strongly influenced by means-testing and that the relationship between insurance and informal care can change dramatically depending on the way means-testing is structured.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between public LTC support, private insurance and informal care, which are all important components of a comprehensive policy for LTC.
the interaction of public LTC support and private LTC insurance.
the following question: how does means-testing influence the interaction between LTC insurance and formal care?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of a means-tested public LTC support scheme, insurance and informal care interact in a complex way.
the optimal level of informal care is increasing in the degree of generosity of public support for LTC, while the optimal level of insurance is decreasing.

the more the means-test structure of public support takes into account LTC needs and the more it considers the insurance benefits, the more it is likely that the relationship between LTC and informal care is enhanced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of public means-tested support for LTC has a significant impact on the relationship between LTC and informal care, as well as on the level of informal care.
the means-tested public support should consider both the cost of LTC and the insurance benefits.
the optimal level of insurance is higher and the optimal level of informal care is lower if the public means-tested support considers the insurance benefits of the recipient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
means-tested public support should be structured in ways that are consistent with the objective of promoting informal care.
the optimal level of insurance and informal LTC is not necessarily the highest level of insurance and the lowest level of informal care.
means-tested public support can be designed so as to reduce the incentives to purchase LTC insurance and to provide informal care.
